import numpy as np
from scipy import stats
from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
from collections import defaultdict

MAX_DRIVERS = 4

def design(feats):
    # Check for association with outcome
    effects = []
    for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
        if feats.types[i] == 'clinical':
            # For clinical features, use t-test
            y0 = feats.x[feats.y==0, i]
            y1 = feats.x[feats.y==1, i]
            t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
        else:
            # For other features, use correlation
            t_stat = np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, i], feats.y)[0, 1]
        effects.append((abs(t_stat), fid))
    
    # Sort by effect size
    effects.sort(reverse=True)
    
    # Check for stratification consistency
    stratum_effects = defaultdict(list)
    for stratum in set(feats.stratum):
        mask = [s == stratum for s in feats.stratum]
        stratum_y = feats.y[mask]
        stratum_x = feats.x[mask]
        
        for i, fid in enumerate(feats.ids):
            if feats.types[i] == 'clinical':
                y0 = stratum_x[stratum_y==0, i]
                y1 = stratum_x[stratum_y==1, i]
                t_stat, _ = stats.ttest_ind(y0, y1, equal_var=False)
            else:
                t_stat = np.corrcoef(stratum_x[:, i], stratum_y)[0, 1]
            stratum_effects[fid].append(abs(t_stat))
    
    # Filter features that show consistent effect across strata
    consistent_features = []
    for fid in feats.ids:
        if len(stratum_effects[fid]) > 1:
            std_dev = np.std(stratum_effects[fid])
            mean_effect = np.mean(stratum_effects[fid])
            if mean_effect > 0.1 and std_dev / mean_effect < 0.5:  # Consistent effect
                consistent_features.append(fid)
    
    # Find top features
    top_features = [fid for _, fid in effects[:10]]
    
    # Check for near-duplicates and remove them
    to_remove = set()
    for i, fid1 in enumerate(top_features):
        for j, fid2 in enumerate(top_features[i+1:], i+1):
            col1 = feats.column(fid1)
            col2 = feats.column(fid2)
            if abs(np.corrcoef(feats.x[:, col1], feats.x[:, col2])[0, 1]) > 0.6:
                to_remove.add(fid2)
    
    filtered_features = [fid for fid in top_features if fid not in to_remove]
    
    # Select best features for model
    selected_features = filtered_features[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # Check if any features have strong enough effect to be drivers
    drivers = []
    if selected_features:
        # Fit logistic regression to check significance
        X = feats.x[:, [feats.column(fid) for fid in selected_features]]
        model = LogisticRegression(penalty='l1', solver='liblinear', C=0.1)
        model.fit(X, feats.y)
        
        # Get coefficients and check if they're significant
        coef = model.coef_[0]
        if any(abs(c) > 0.1 for c in coef):  # At least one coefficient is large
            # Use effect sizes to prioritize drivers
            drivers = [fid for _, fid in effects if fid in selected_features][:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    # If we have drivers, include all features that are part of the model
    if drivers:
        columns = selected_features
        products = []
        loadings = {}
        for i, fid in enumerate(columns):
            col_idx = feats.column(fid)
            # Weighted loading based on effect size
            loadings[fid] = effects[i][0] if i < len(effects) else 1.0
    else:
        # No mechanism found
        return Design(drivers=(), columns=(), products=(), loadings={})
    
    # Ensure we don't exceed MAX_DRIVERS
    if len(drivers) > MAX_DRIVERS:
        drivers = drivers[:MAX_DRIVERS]
    
    return Design(drivers=tuple(drivers), columns=tuple(columns), products=tuple(products), loadings=loadings)
